title: CLIOPATRA: Extracting Private Information from LLM Insights
claim: A multi-stage insights system turns raw user conversations into aggregated summaries through successive protective filtering and abstraction stages.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, tall hatched filter bars between data stages
description: A single horizontal flow diagram drawn in a hand-written, whiteboard-like font. Four data stages run left to right, each a stack of colored rounded bars with an ellipsis between the top and bottom groups. Red bars are conversations, blue bars are facets, blue bars grouped inside yellow-orange rounded boxes are clusters, and green bars are cluster summaries. Between the stages sit tall pink hatched rounded rectangles that act as processing or filter modules, each with a black arrow passing through it. Labels sit above and below these modules. Facet Extraction is paired with Remove PII, Clustering has no module, Summarization is paired with Drop Small Clusters, and Privacy Audit is paired with Filter Suspicious Summaries. The eye goes first to the colored bar stacks and the arrows.

abstract: The widespread adoption of AI assistants has encouraged the development of privacy-aware platforms designed to extract insights from real-world usage. Their privacy protections primarily rely on layering multiple heuristic techniques, such as PII redaction, clustering, aggregation, and LLM-based privacy auditing. In this paper, we put their privacy claims to the test by presenting CLIOPATRA, the first attack against "privacy-preserving" LLM-based insights systems. Our attack involves an adversary that carefully designs and inserts malicious chats into the system to break multiple layers of protections and induce the leakage of sensitive information from a target user's chat. We evaluate CLIOPATRA on one such platform, Anthropic's Clio (now called "Anthropic Insights"), and target synthetically generated medical chats to show that an adversary can successfully and confidently (with nearly 100% precision) extract the medical history contained in these chats in up to 65% of cases. We also show that CLIOPATRA can stealthily extract information by obfuscating the private information in the generated insights. Finally, we demonstrate that existing ad hoc mitigations, such as LLM-based privacy auditing, are unreliable and fail to detect major leaks. Overall, our findings indicate that, even when layered, current heuristic protections are insufficient to adequately protect user data, and that prompt injection has been an understudied risk in LLM-based insight systems.
